title: How much shielding protects lunar crews from solar storms
licence: U.S. Government work (no U.S. copyright); free to use with credit
citation: Clowdsley, M. (2021) Protecting Astronauts from Space Radiation on the Lunar Surface, Lunar Surface Innovation Consortium, 9 Feb 2021.
boundary: 20 g/cm2 is Clowdsley's target against galactic cosmic rays (GCR; slides 16, 31). For solar storms, Townsend, Nealy & Wilson 1988 (NASA-TM-100620, NTRS 19880016043, p. 4) found 20 g/cm2 of water keeps the largest recorded flares under the 30-day limit. Slide 37 is a rover storm-shelter model for a female astronaut; dose never reaches zero. Game zaps are not mSv.
